summary: August Sundin is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied as a PhD student at Ghent University and served as a faculty member there, both attested in 2026.

August Tholuck (1799–1877) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1816–1820). He later held posts at Berlin (circa 1821–1826) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (circa 1826–1877).

August Wilhelm von Schlegel (1767–1845) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne, and later under Antoine-Léonard Chézy and Alexander Hamilton. He held professorships at Jena (1795, 1798) and Bonn (1818).

Auguste Barth (1834–1916) was an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a licence at the University of Strasbourg (circa 1853–1856). He held posts at Collège Poincaré Saverne and was a member of the Institut de France.
Auguste Comte (1798–1857) was a philosopher. He studied at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and then at École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle (1841–1918) specialized in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as director of Calcutta Madrasa (circa 1881–1899) and as Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society in 1891.

Aung San Suu Kyi (born 1945) works in Tibetology and other fields. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, University of Delhi, St Hugh's College, and SOAS, and held a post at the United Nations (circa 1969–1971).

Awadh Kishore Narain (1925–2013) was a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later holding major professorial and administrative posts at Banaras Hindu University and Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Axel Klein (born 1968) specializes in Japanology. He studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994) and held posts there (1998–2007), at the German Institute for Japanese Studies (2007–2011), and at the University of Duisburg-Essen (2012).

Axel Michaels (born 1949), an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at the University of Hamburg and Kiel University. He held posts at Kiel, served as Director of the Nepal Research Centre, and was professor at Bern and Heidelberg.
Ayako Nakamura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed her PhD at the University of Hamburg (attested 2009) and later served there as a research fellow (attested 2026).

Ayinapalli Aiyappan (1905–1988) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Madras and held posts as Superintendent of the Government Museum, Chennai (circa 1940–1960) and at the University of Kerala (circa 1969–1971).

Ayu Khandro (1839–1953) was a figure in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under masters including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Nyala Pema Dündul, Chokgyur Lingpa, and Drodul Pawo Dorje.
Ayush Maheshwari is a scholar in computational fields and Indology. He completed his PhD at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay and held a post there.

Ayya Khema (1923–1997) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. She studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Mahathera, and Matara Sri Nyanarama, and held a teaching post at Buddha-Haus in 1989.
Azizah Nur is a doctoral student at the Australian National University, studying under doctoral supervisor Assa Doron (attested 2026).

B. Alan Wallace (born 1950) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst and Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt, taught at Rabten Choeling, and held a lectureship at UC Santa Barbara (circa 1997–2001).

B. N. Goswamy (1933–2023) was an art historian and Indologist. He studied at Panjab University (circa 1950–1961), worked in the Indian Administrative Service (circa 1956–1958), and held a post at Panjab University (circa 1965–1993).

B. N. K. Sharma (1909–2005) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Madras and under Satyadhyana Tirtha, serving in posts at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, and Ramnarain Ruia College (1953–1969).

B. R. Ambedkar (1891–1956) was a scholar of religion and philosophy. Educated at Columbia, LSE, and the University of London, his academic posts included professorships at Sydenham College and serving as principal of Government Law College, Mumbai.
